questions.q: What formula does Fuhrman use to define health?
a: Health equals nutrients divided by calories
Health equals calories divided by nutrients
Health equals exercise plus calorie restriction
Health equals protein plus vitamins minus fat
questions.why: Lesson 2 reduces healthy eating to nutrient density: health equals nutrients divided by calories.

questions.q: How many calories fit in a stomach full of meat and cheese?
a: About 3,000
About 1,000
About 500
About 200
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a stomach holding a liter of calorie-dense meat and cheese would contain around 3,000 calories.

questions.q: How many calories does a liter of fruit and vegetables provide?
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts the 3,000 calories of meat and cheese with the 200 to 500 calories in a liter of produce.

questions.q: Which foods have the highest nutrient density in the summary?
a: Fruits, beans, legumes and green vegetables
Whole grains, dairy and lean meat
Nuts, seeds and vegetable oils
Eggs, fish and poultry
questions.why: Lesson 2 says fruits, beans, legumes and green vegetables score 50 to 100 on nutrient density, far above refined sweets at 0.

questions.q: What is the core problem with the processed foods in most modern diets?
a: They deliver calories without the nutrients the body needs
They contain too little fat to satisfy hunger
They are more expensive than fresh produce
They spoil faster than unprocessed ingredients
questions.why: Lesson 1 estimates that 62 percent of American calories come from processed carbohydrates and oils that provide energy without nutrients.
